2597:     /// there are active readers because the existence of `HalfPerm` resource for read access.
2598:     /// If it is `Right`, we know there is an active writer and there is no active reader, because there is a `NoPerm`

2602:     /// the number of `try_read` increments recorded in the lock atomic and the number of active
2603:     /// `RwLockReadGuard`s (created and ongoing creation that will succeed) represented by `read_guard_token`.

2605:     /// which allows at most `2*MAX_READER - 1` `try_read` attempts that will fail to acquire the lock.

2702: struct_with_invariants! {
2703: /// Spin-based Read-write Lock
2704: ///
2705: /// # Overview
2706: ///
2707: /// This lock allows for multiple readers, or at most one writer to access
2708: /// at any point in time. The writer of this lock has exclusive access to
2709: /// modify the underlying data, while the readers are allowed shared and
2710: /// read-only access.
2711: ///
2712: /// The writing and reading portions cannot be active simultaneously, when
2713: /// one portion is in progress, the other portion will spin-wait. This is
2714: /// suitable for scenarios where the lock is expected to be held for short
2715: /// periods of time, and the overhead of context switching is higher than
2716: /// the cost of spinning.
2717: ///
2718: /// In addition to traditional read and write locks, this implementation
2719: /// provides the upgradeable read lock (`upread lock`). The `upread lock`
2720: /// can be upgraded to write locks atomically, useful in scenarios
2721: /// where a decision to write is made after reading.
2722: ///
2723: /// The type parameter `T` represents the data that this lock is protecting.
2724: /// It is necessary for `T` to satisfy [`Send`] to be shared across tasks and
2725: /// [`Sync`] to permit concurrent access via readers. The [`Deref`] method (and
2726: /// [`DerefMut`] for the writer) is implemented for the RAII guards returned
2727: /// by the locking methods, which allows for the access to the protected data
2728: /// while the lock is held.
2729: ///
2730: /// # Usage
2731: /// The lock can be used in scenarios where data needs to be read frequently
2732: /// but written to occasionally.
2733: ///
2734: /// Use `upread lock` in scenarios where related checking is performed before
2735: /// modification to effectively avoid deadlocks and improve efficiency.
2736: ///
2737: /// This lock should not be used in scenarios where lock-holding times are
2738: /// long as it can lead to CPU resource wastage due to spinning.
2739: ///
2740: /// # About Guard
2741: ///
2742: /// See the comments of [`SpinLock`].
2743: ///
2744: /// # Examples
2745: ///
2746: /// ```
2747: /// use ostd::sync::RwLock;
2748: ///
2749: /// let lock = RwLock::new(5)
2750: ///
2751: /// // many read locks can be held at once
2752: /// {
2753: ///     let r1 = lock.read();
2754: ///     let r2 = lock.read();
2755: ///     assert_eq!(*r1, 5);
2756: ///     assert_eq!(*r2, 5);
2757: ///
2758: ///     // Upgradeable read lock can share access to data with read locks
2759: ///     let r3 = lock.upread();
2760: ///     assert_eq!(*r3, 5);
2761: ///     drop(r1);
2762: ///     drop(r2);
2763: ///     // read locks are dropped at this point
2764: ///
2765: ///     // An upread lock can only be upgraded successfully after all the
2766: ///     // read locks are released, otherwise it will spin-wait.
2767: ///     let mut w1 = r3.upgrade();
2768: ///     *w1 += 1;
2769: ///     assert_eq!(*w1, 6);
2770: /// }   // upread lock are dropped at this point
2771: ///
2772: /// {
2773: ///     // Only one write lock can be held at a time
2774: ///     let mut w2 = lock.write();
2775: ///     *w2 += 1;
2776: ///     assert_eq!(*w2, 7);
2777: /// }   // write lock is dropped at this point
2778: /// ```
2779: ///
2780: /// [`SpinLock`]: super::SpinLock
2781: pub struct RwLock<T  /* : ?Sized*/ , Guard /* = PreemptDisabled*/ > {
2782:     guard: PhantomData<Guard>,
2783:     /// The internal representation of the lock state is as follows:
2784:     /// - **Bit 63:** Writer lock.
2785:     /// - **Bit 62:** Upgradeable reader lock.
2786:     /// - **Bit 61:** Indicates if an upgradeable reader is being upgraded.
2787:     /// - **Bits 60-0:** Reader lock count.
2788:     lock: AtomicUsize<_, RwPerms<T>,_>,
2789:     // val: UnsafeCell<T>,
2790:     val: PCell<T>,
2791:     ghost_id: Ghost<RwId>,
2792: }
2793: 
2794: /// This invariant holds at any time, i.e. not violated during any method execution.
2795: closed spec fn wf(self) -> bool {
2796:     invariant on lock with (val, guard, ghost_id) is (v: usize, g: RwPerms<T>) {
2797:         // BITS VALUE
2798:         let has_writer_bit: bool = (v & WRITER) != 0;
2799:         let has_upgrade_bit: bool = (v & UPGRADEABLE_READER) != 0;
2800:         let has_max_reader_bit: bool = (v & MAX_READER) != 0;
2801:         // The total number of `try_read` attempts recorded in the lock atomic, including created `RwLockReadGuard`s
2802:         // and those who are trying, no matter they will succeed or fail.
2803:         let total_reader_bits: int = (v & MAX_READER_MASK) as int;
2804:         // The clamped value represented in the counter bits. This counts the maximum number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2805:         // NOTE: This does not mean there are actually this number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s. The actual number of successfully
2806:         // created/creating `RwLockReadGuard`s can be smaller than this number, because previously created `RwLockReadGuard`s may be dropped.
2807:         let reader_bits: int = if has_max_reader_bit { MAX_READER as int } else { (v & READER_MASK) as int };
2808: 
2809:         // ACTUAL NUMBER OF ACTIVE GUARDS.
2810:         // The number is tracked by the ghost resources remained in the lock.
2811:         // By active, we mean from the perspective the lock, the permissions for these guards are given out.
2812:         // The actual guards may be still being created, but they must be successfully created finally.
2813:         // This invariant maintains the consistency between the ghost resources and the lock atomic value.
2814: 
2815:         // Whether there is an active writer
2816:         let active_writer: bool = g.core_token.is_right();
2817:         // The number of active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`, which can only be 0 or 1.
2818:         let active_upgrade_guard: bool = !active_writer && g.upreader_guard_token is None;
2819:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2820:         let active_read_guards: int = if g.read_guard_token is Left {
2821:             MAX_READER_U64 - g.read_guard_token.left().frac()
2822:         } else {
2823:             0
2824:         };
2825:         // The first `try_upread` that fails, which has not returned yet.
2826:         let pending_failed_upread_attempt: bool = g.upread_retract_token is None;
2827:         // The number of `try_read` attempts that will fail.
2828:         let failed_reader_attempts: int = V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS - g.read_retract_token.frac();
2829: 
2830:         &&& if g.core_token.is_left() {
2831:             g.read_guard_token is Left
2832:         } else {
2833:             &&& g.upreader_guard_token is None
2834:             &&& g.read_guard_token is Right
2835:         }
2836:         // The `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit is set iff there is an active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` or a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2837:         &&& has_upgrade_bit <==> (active_upgrade_guard || pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2838:         // An active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` cannot coexist with a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2839:         &&& !(active_upgrade_guard && pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2840:         // The `READER` bits count the number of all active read guards and pending failed `try_read` attempts.
2841:         &&& total_reader_bits == active_read_guards + failed_reader_attempts
2842:         // There is an active `RwLockWriteGuard` iff the `WRITER` bit is set.
2843:         &&& active_writer <==> has_writer_bit
2844:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGaurd`s is less than or equal to the `READER` bits.
2845:         &&& 0 <= active_read_guards <= reader_bits <= total_reader_bits
2846:         // The core invariant of `RwLock`: there are no simultaneous active writers and readers.
2847:         &&& !(active_writer && (active_read_guards + if active_upgrade_guard { 1int } else { 0 }) > 0)
2848:         &&& g.core_token.id() == ghost_id@.core_token_id
2849:         &&& g.core_token.wf()
2850:         &&& g.core_token.is_left() ==> {
2851:             &&& !g.core_token.is_resource_owner()
2852:             &&& g.core_token.frac() == 1
2853:         }
2854:         &&& g.core_token.is_right() ==> {
2855:             let empty = g.core_token.resource_right();
2856:             &&& empty.id() == ghost_id@.frac_id
2857:             &&& g.core_token.frac() == 2
2858:             &&& g.core_token.has_resource()
2859:         }
2860:         &&& g.read_retract_token.wf()
2861:         &&& g.read_retract_token.id() == ghost_id@.read_retract_token_id
2862:         &&& g.upread_retract_token is Some ==>
2863:             {
2864:                 let token = g.upread_retract_token->0;
2865:                 &&& token.wf()
2866:                 &&& token.id() == ghost_id@.upread_retract_token_id
2867:             }
2868:         &&& g.upreader_guard_token is Some ==> {
2869:             let token = g.upreader_guard_token->0;
2870:             wf_upgradeable_guard_token(ghost_id@.core_token_id, ghost_id@.frac_id, val.id(), token)
2871:         }
2872:         &&& match g.read_guard_token {
2873:             Sum::Left(token) => {
2874:                 &&& token.wf()
2875:                 &&& token.id() == ghost_id@.read_guard_token_id
2876:                 &&& token.not_empty() ==> {
2877:                     let resource = token.resource();
2878:                     let read_half_cell_perm = resource.0;
2879:                     let mode_knowledge = resource.1;
2880:                     &&& mode_knowledge.id() == ghost_id@.core_token_id
2881:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.id() == ghost_id@.frac_id
2882:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.resource().id() == val.id()
2883:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.frac() == 1
2884:                 }
2885:             },
2886:             Sum::Right(empty) => {
2887:                 &&& empty.id() == ghost_id@.read_guard_token_id
2888:             },
2889:         }
2890: 
2891:     }
2892: }
2893: 
2894: }

2988:     /// Acquires a read lock and spin-wait until it can be acquired.
2989:     ///
2990:     /// The calling thread will spin-wait until there are no writers or
2991:     /// upgrading upreaders present. There is no guarantee for the order
2992:     /// in which other readers or writers waiting simultaneously will
2993:     /// obtain the lock.
2994:     #[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]
2995:     pub fn read(&self) -> RwLockReadGuard<'_, T, G> {
2996:         loop {
2997:             if let Some(readguard) = self.try_read() {
2998:                 return readguard;
2999:             } else {
3000:                 core::hint::spin_loop();
3001:             }
3002:         }
3003:     }

3005:     /// Acquires a write lock and spin-wait until it can be acquired.
3006:     ///
3007:     /// The calling thread will spin-wait until there are no other writers,
3008:     /// upreaders or readers present. There is no guarantee for the order
3009:     /// in which other readers or writers waiting simultaneously will
3010:     /// obtain the lock.
3011:     #[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]
3012:     pub fn write(&self) -> RwLockWriteGuard<'_, T, G> {
3013:         loop {
3014:             if let Some(writeguard) = self.try_write() {

2585: /// The token reserved in the lock when the write permission is given out.
2586: type NoPerm<T> = EmptyCount<PointsTo<T>>;
2587: type NoPermU64 = EmptyCount<u64>;
2588: 
2589: /// Half of the permission for read access, one for `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` and the other for all `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2590: type HalfPerm<T> = Count<PointsTo<T>>;
2591: type HalfPermU64 = Count<u64>;
2592: 
2593: /// The permission for read access can be further split into `MAX_READER` pieces.
2594: type ReadPerm<T> = (HalfPerm<T>, OneLeftKnowledge<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>);
2595: 
2596: tracked struct RwPerms<T> {
2597:     /// This token tracks whether the write permission is given out. If it is `Left`, it stores the knowledge that
2598:     /// there are active readers because the existence of `HalfPerm` resource for read access.
2599:     /// If it is `Right`, we know there is an active writer and there is no active reader, because there is a `NoPerm`
2600:     /// indicating the absence of `PointsTo<T>`.
2601:     core_token: SumResource<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>,
2602:     /// The permission to retract a `READER` count. Its total quantity tracks the gap between
2603:     /// the number of `try_read` increments recorded in the lock atomic and the number of active
2604:     /// `RwLockReadGuard`s (created and ongoing creation that will succeed) represented by `read_guard_token`.
2605:     /// It can be splited up to `V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS:= 2 * MAX_READER` pieces,
2606:     /// which allows at most `2*MAX_READER - 1` `try_read` attempts that will fail to acquire the lock.
2607:     read_retract_token: TokenResource<V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS>,
2608:     /// The permission to retract the set of `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit.
2609:     upread_retract_token: Option<UniqueToken>,
2610:     /// Tracks whether there is a live `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`, also stores half of the permission for read access.
2611:     upreader_guard_token: Option<OneLeftOwner<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>>,
2612:     /// Tracks the number of live `RwLockReadGuard`s. If it is `Left`, it stores the remaining read permissions.
2613:     /// If it is `Right`, it stores an empty token indicating the permission has been given out.
2614:     read_guard_token: Sum<
2615:         CountResource<ReadPerm<T>, MAX_READER_U64>,
2616:         EmptyCount<ReadPerm<T>, MAX_READER_U64>,
2617:     >,
2618: }
2619:

2621:     core_token_id: Loc,
2622:     frac_id: Loc,
2623:     read_retract_token_id: Loc,
2624:     upread_retract_token_id: Loc,
2625:     read_guard_token_id: Loc,

2628: /// The number of `try_read` operations recorded in the lock atomic (created and ongoing) can never reach `2*MAX_READER` to avoid overflow.
2629: /// **NOTE**: We *ASSUME* this property always holds without any proof. We believe this is true in practice because:
2630: /// - More than `2^61` `try_read` operations are required to trigger the overflow concurrently, which is absurd in real world scenarios.
2631: /// - If one tries to create a huge number (more than `2*MAX_READER`) of `RwLockReadGuard`s in a loop with `mem::forget`, it will take years and
2632: /// will be prevented by the `MAX_READER` check.
2633: pub closed spec fn no_max_reader_overflow(v: usize) -> bool {
2634:     v & MAX_READER_MASK < MAX_READER_MASK
2635: }

2703: struct_with_invariants! {
2704: /// Spin-based Read-write Lock
2705: ///
2706: /// # Overview
2707: ///
2708: /// This lock allows for multiple readers, or at most one writer to access
2709: /// at any point in time. The writer of this lock has exclusive access to
2710: /// modify the underlying data, while the readers are allowed shared and
2711: /// read-only access.
2712: ///
2713: /// The writing and reading portions cannot be active simultaneously, when
2714: /// one portion is in progress, the other portion will spin-wait. This is
2715: /// suitable for scenarios where the lock is expected to be held for short
2716: /// periods of time, and the overhead of context switching is higher than
2717: /// the cost of spinning.
2718: ///
2719: /// In addition to traditional read and write locks, this implementation
2720: /// provides the upgradeable read lock (`upread lock`). The `upread lock`
2721: /// can be upgraded to write locks atomically, useful in scenarios
2722: /// where a decision to write is made after reading.
2723: ///
2724: /// The type parameter `T` represents the data that this lock is protecting.
2725: /// It is necessary for `T` to satisfy [`Send`] to be shared across tasks and
2726: /// [`Sync`] to permit concurrent access via readers. The [`Deref`] method (and
2727: /// [`DerefMut`] for the writer) is implemented for the RAII guards returned
2728: /// by the locking methods, which allows for the access to the protected data
2729: /// while the lock is held.
2730: ///
2731: /// # Usage
2732: /// The lock can be used in scenarios where data needs to be read frequently
2733: /// but written to occasionally.
2734: ///
2735: /// Use `upread lock` in scenarios where related checking is performed before
2736: /// modification to effectively avoid deadlocks and improve efficiency.
2737: ///
2738: /// This lock should not be used in scenarios where lock-holding times are
2739: /// long as it can lead to CPU resource wastage due to spinning.
2740: ///
2741: /// # About Guard
2742: ///
2743: /// See the comments of [`SpinLock`].
2744: ///
2745: /// # Examples
2746: ///
2747: /// ```
2748: /// use ostd::sync::RwLock;
2749: ///
2750: /// let lock = RwLock::new(5)
2751: ///
2752: /// // many read locks can be held at once
2753: /// {
2754: ///     let r1 = lock.read();
2755: ///     let r2 = lock.read();
2756: ///     assert_eq!(*r1, 5);
2757: ///     assert_eq!(*r2, 5);
2758: ///
2759: ///     // Upgradeable read lock can share access to data with read locks
2760: ///     let r3 = lock.upread();
2761: ///     assert_eq!(*r3, 5);
2762: ///     drop(r1);
2763: ///     drop(r2);
2764: ///     // read locks are dropped at this point
2765: ///
2766: ///     // An upread lock can only be upgraded successfully after all the
2767: ///     // read locks are released, otherwise it will spin-wait.
2768: ///     let mut w1 = r3.upgrade();
2769: ///     *w1 += 1;
2770: ///     assert_eq!(*w1, 6);
2771: /// }   // upread lock are dropped at this point
2772: ///
2773: /// {
2774: ///     // Only one write lock can be held at a time
2775: ///     let mut w2 = lock.write();
2776: ///     *w2 += 1;
2777: ///     assert_eq!(*w2, 7);
2778: /// }   // write lock is dropped at this point
2779: /// ```
2780: ///
2781: /// [`SpinLock`]: super::SpinLock
2782: pub struct RwLock<T  /* : ?Sized*/ , Guard /* = PreemptDisabled*/ > {
2783:     guard: PhantomData<Guard>,
2784:     /// The internal representation of the lock state is as follows:
2785:     /// - **Bit 63:** Writer lock.
2786:     /// - **Bit 62:** Upgradeable reader lock.
2787:     /// - **Bit 61:** Indicates if an upgradeable reader is being upgraded.
2788:     /// - **Bits 60-0:** Reader lock count.
2789:     lock: AtomicUsize<_, RwPerms<T>,_>,
2790:     // val: UnsafeCell<T>,
2791:     val: PCell<T>,
2792:     ghost_id: Ghost<RwId>,
2793: }
2794: 
2795: /// This invariant holds at any time, i.e. not violated during any method execution.
2796: closed spec fn wf(self) -> bool {
2797:     invariant on lock with (val, guard, ghost_id) is (v: usize, g: RwPerms<T>) {
2798:         // BITS VALUE
2799:         let has_writer_bit: bool = (v & WRITER) != 0;
2800:         let has_upgrade_bit: bool = (v & UPGRADEABLE_READER) != 0;
2801:         let has_max_reader_bit: bool = (v & MAX_READER) != 0;
2802:         // The total number of `try_read` attempts recorded in the lock atomic, including created `RwLockReadGuard`s
2803:         // and those who are trying, no matter they will succeed or fail.
2804:         let total_reader_bits: int = (v & MAX_READER_MASK) as int;
2805:         // The clamped value represented in the counter bits. This counts the maximum number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2806:         // NOTE: This does not mean there are actually this number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s. The actual number of successfully
2807:         // created/creating `RwLockReadGuard`s can be smaller than this number, because previously created `RwLockReadGuard`s may be dropped.
2808:         let reader_bits: int = if has_max_reader_bit { MAX_READER as int } else { (v & READER_MASK) as int };
2809: 
2810:         // ACTUAL NUMBER OF ACTIVE GUARDS.
2811:         // The number is tracked by the ghost resources remained in the lock.
2812:         // By active, we mean from the perspective the lock, the permissions for these guards are given out.
2813:         // The actual guards may be still being created, but they must be successfully created finally.
2814:         // This invariant maintains the consistency between the ghost resources and the lock atomic value.
2815: 
2816:         // Whether there is an active writer
2817:         let active_writer: bool = g.core_token.is_right();
2818:         // The number of active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`, which can only be 0 or 1.
2819:         let active_upgrade_guard: bool = !active_writer && g.upreader_guard_token is None;
2820:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2821:         let active_read_guards: int = if g.read_guard_token is Left {
2822:             MAX_READER_U64 - g.read_guard_token.left().frac()
2823:         } else {
2824:             0
2825:         };
2826:         // The first `try_upread` that fails, which has not returned yet.
2827:         let pending_failed_upread_attempt: bool = g.upread_retract_token is None;
2828:         // The number of `try_read` attempts that will fail.
2829:         let failed_reader_attempts: int = V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS - g.read_retract_token.frac();
2830: 
2831:         &&& if g.core_token.is_left() {
2832:             g.read_guard_token is Left
2833:         } else {
2834:             &&& g.upreader_guard_token is None
2835:             &&& g.read_guard_token is Right
2836:         }
2837:         // The `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit is set iff there is an active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` or a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2838:         &&& has_upgrade_bit <==> (active_upgrade_guard || pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2839:         // An active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` cannot coexist with a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2840:         &&& !(active_upgrade_guard && pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2841:         // The `READER` bits count the number of all active read guards and pending failed `try_read` attempts.
2842:         &&& total_reader_bits == active_read_guards + failed_reader_attempts
2843:         // There is an active `RwLockWriteGuard` iff the `WRITER` bit is set.
2844:         &&& active_writer <==> has_writer_bit
2845:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGaurd`s is less than or equal to the `READER` bits.
2846:         &&& 0 <= active_read_guards <= reader_bits <= total_reader_bits
2847:         // The core invariant of `RwLock`: there are no simultaneous active writers and readers.
2848:         &&& !(active_writer && (active_read_guards + if active_upgrade_guard { 1int } else { 0 }) > 0)
2849:         &&& g.core_token.id() == ghost_id@.core_token_id
2850:         &&& g.core_token.wf()
2851:         &&& g.core_token.is_left() ==> {
2852:             &&& !g.core_token.is_resource_owner()
2853:             &&& g.core_token.frac() == 1
2854:         }
2855:         &&& g.core_token.is_right() ==> {
2856:             let empty = g.core_token.resource_right();
2857:             &&& empty.id() == ghost_id@.frac_id
2858:             &&& g.core_token.frac() == 2
2859:             &&& g.core_token.has_resource()
2860:         }
2861:         &&& g.read_retract_token.wf()
2862:         &&& g.read_retract_token.id() == ghost_id@.read_retract_token_id
2863:         &&& g.upread_retract_token is Some ==> {
2864:             let token = g.upread_retract_token->0;
2865:             &&& token.wf()
